candidate_analysis.explanation: The Random Forest classifies this binary as malware with probability 0.95, and all 20 top SHAP features push toward cryptojacking. None pull the other way. The strongest signals are SIMD bitwise and integer-vector sequences: PXOR MOVAPS (+0.0197, rank 1), MOVDQA PAND (+0.0097), PXOR MOVUPS (+0.0095), PAND PXOR (+0.0063) and PADDQ MOVDQA (+0.0058). These are typical of vectorized mixing, masking and 64-bit lane arithmetic in hash or proof-of-work inner loops. A second cluster is rotate/shift/add arithmetic: ROL ADD (+0.0092), ADD ROR (+0.0075), ADD ROL (+0.0055), SHRD XOR (+0.0073) and SHL NEG (+0.0062). This is the ARX-style (add-rotate-xor) and multi-word shift-and-mix arithmetic used in hash and cipher rounds. SUB ADC (+0.0079) suggests multi-precision arithmetic with carry propagation, and MOVAPD DIVSD (+0.0061) suggests some floating-point work. The remaining n-grams (ADD PUSH, POP LEA, PUSH RET, CALL RET, CALL PUSH, POP PUSH, SUB CMOVG, SHL XCHG) are generic control-flow, stack or arithmetic patterns. They add modest support, likely from the compiled code structure around a compute kernel. Caveats: no function names, API calls or strings were provided, so the evidence is purely statistical and indirect. The same instruction mixes also occur in legitimate cryptographic libraries. Each n-gram has a very low relative frequency (at most 0.00043). Even so, the breadth of consistent crypto-style compute signatures and the high model probability make a cryptojacking classification well supported.
